# Draft a Polite but Firm Refund Email with Le Chat

> **In short:** Le Chat, Mistral's AI assistant, can turn a messy complaint into a calm, clear refund request in a few minutes. You describe what went wrong and what you want back; the assistant shapes it into a respectful email. You'll still review, personalize and send the message yourself from your own email account.

If a product arrived broken, a service didn't deliver what was promised, or a charge looks wrong, the hardest part is often just writing the email. You want to be firm enough to be taken seriously, but polite enough that the person reading it on the other end actually wants to help. That's exactly the kind of writing Le Chat is good at shaping. This guide walks you through it, start to finish, in roughly ten minutes.

## Before you start
- A free or paid Le Chat account. Mistral says Le Chat has a free tier with a daily message limit and paid plans for heavier use; check the current tiers on Mistral's site before you start.
- Access to Le Chat in your browser (go to chat.mistral.ai) or through the official app.
- The key facts about your case: order or invoice number, what you bought, when, what went wrong, and what you'd like the company to do (refund, replacement, repair, credit).
- Roughly 10 minutes.

## Step 1 — Open Le Chat and start a fresh conversation

Go to **chat.mistral.ai** in your browser, or open the Le Chat app on your phone. If you're not already signed in, log in with the Mistral account you created. Once you're on the main chat screen, look for a **"New chat"** button, a **pencil icon**, or a **plus (+) sign** — these are common ways to start a clean conversation. Click or tap it so you have an empty chat box ready.

💬 Example: you don't need to type anything yet. Just click the button that starts a new chat.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows an empty message box with no previous conversation in the list, and any old chats are out of the way. Starting fresh matters because Le Chat only uses what you put in *this* conversation, so an empty box means nothing will confuse the reply.

## Step 2 — Tell Le Chat what happened, in plain words

In the empty message box, write a short, honest description of what went wrong. Don't try to make it sound polite yet — that's Le Chat's job. Just give the facts in a few sentences: what you bought, when, what was supposed to happen, what actually happened, and how you found out. Think of it like writing a quick note to a friend, not a letter to a lawyer.

💬 Example: "I bought a noise-canceling headphone set from AudioBrand on October 12, order #44291, for $189. It was supposed to arrive by October 19. It arrived on October 24 in a damaged box, and the right ear cup doesn't work. AudioBrand support replied once and then stopped responding."

You'll know it worked when Le Chat confirms it understands the situation, usually by restating the key facts back to you in one or two sentences. If the assistant seems to have misunderstood something, just reply with a short correction ("no, it was the headphones, not the charger") before moving on.

## Step 3 — Tell Le Chat the tone you want

Right after describing the problem, in the same message or in a follow-up, tell Le Chat how you want the email to sound. The trick is to name the tone in everyday words: "polite but firm" works well, but so do phrases like "respectful and clear," "calm but serious," or "friendly but I want a real answer, not a brush-off." Also tell Le Chat who you are to the company — a regular customer, a long-time subscriber, whoever fits — so the tone matches.

💬 Example: "Now please turn this into a refund request email. Keep the tone polite but firm — I'm a regular customer who's been patient, but I want a real resolution, not a generic reply. Don't threaten legal action. Keep it under 200 words."

You'll know it worked when Le Chat produces a short, readable email draft with a greeting, a clear statement of the problem, and a specific ask at the end. If the draft feels too soft or too aggressive, you can simply say "a bit firmer, please" or "softer please" and Le Chat will adjust in the next message.

## Step 4 — Add the missing details Le Chat should include

Most refund requests get ignored or delayed because the reader on the company's side doesn't have enough information to act. Look at Le Chat's draft and check whether it includes: your name, the order or invoice number, the date of purchase, what the product or service was, what went wrong, what you want (full refund, partial credit, replacement), and a reasonable deadline for a reply. If anything is missing, ask Le Chat to add it.

💬 Example: "Please add my order number (#44291), the date I bought it (October 12), and a line asking for a full refund or a replacement within 7 business days. Also add a short closing sentence thanking them for looking into it."

You'll know it worked when a fresh version of the email appears with those details woven naturally into the text, not pasted in as a random list. If Le Chat puts the details in a weird spot — like the middle of a sentence — tell it where you'd rather see them ("put the order number right after my name").

## Step 5 — Ask Le Chat to give you two versions

Before you settle on a draft, ask Le Chat for one more option that's slightly different. This is a small step that pays off: it gives you something to choose from, and it also lets you see how Le Chat handles the same facts in a different style. You can ask for a "shorter and more direct" version, or a "warmer and more conversational" one.

💬 Example: "Can you give me one more version that's shorter and more direct — about 100 words? Keep the same tone and the same ask."

You'll know it worked when two clearly different drafts are sitting in your chat, and you can spot the small differences in tone and length. Pick the one that feels closest to how you'd actually write, and use the other as a source of small phrases you can borrow (an opening line, a polite but firm closing sentence, a good way to ask for a deadline).

## Step 6 — Personalize the email and send it yourself

Copy your chosen version out of Le Chat into your own email app. Read it once out loud — does it sound like something *you* would say? If anything feels off, change the words. Add a real sign-off with your actual name. Attach any proof you have (a photo of the damaged item, the receipt, the original confirmation email). Then send it from your own email account, addressed to the company's support or billing address — not to Le Chat, since Le Chat can write the email but it can't send it for you.

💬 Example: your finished email might start, "Hi AudioBrand Support team, I'm writing about order #44291, a noise-canceling headphone set I purchased on October 12…"

You'll know it worked when the email in your outbox is calm, specific, and signed with your real name, and the company has everything it needs to act on it. If you don't hear back within the deadline you set, Le Chat can also help you draft a polite follow-up using the same conversation as a reference.

## Common mistakes
- **Sending the AI's draft without reading it.** Le Chat usually writes well, but it doesn't know your real voice. Skim it once, fix anything that doesn't sound like you, and add your name before sending.
- **Leaving out the order number or date.** Customer support can't help with a complaint they can't trace. If your facts aren't in the email, the reply will almost always be "could you provide more details?" — which slows everything down.
- **Asking for a refund without saying what kind.** "I want my money back" is vague. Be specific: full refund, replacement, store credit, or repair. The clearer the ask, the faster the answer.
- **Being rude "to sound firm."** Strong wording is fine; insults or sarcasm aren't. A polite, factual email gets better results than an angry one, even when you're frustrated.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next time a package arrives broken, a subscription overcharges you, or a service quietly stops working, you'll have a ready way to write a calm, effective email in a few minutes instead of staring at a blank screen.
- **For your business or work:** the same prompt style works for vendor disputes, invoice corrections, and client complaints. You describe the situation, name the tone, ask for a clear action, and let the assistant shape the wording.
- **If you're just getting started:** the easiest first move is to paste one short paragraph about a real (or made-up) situation into Le Chat and ask for a polite version. Seeing the result once is the fastest way to learn what the assistant is good at.

## Try it now
Open chat.mistral.ai, start a new chat, and paste a real complaint you actually have (or a short made-up one) followed by: "Turn this into a polite but firm refund request email, under 200 words, that asks for a full refund within 7 business days." Read what comes back — that's the whole skill, in one message.
